gh pr create --repo Juliusolsson05/agent-code --base main --head fix/283-transcript-status-diagnostics --title "debug(#283): instrument transcriptStatus transitions + suspected drop points" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What this is

**Diagnostic instrumentation for #283 — not the fix.** This is the "separate PR" the issue's own _Status_ section calls for: every on-paper ordering preserves the session id, so the stuck-at-`loading` interleaving needs a runtime timeline before fixing at source.

## Background (#283)

On startup (rehydrate) and on resuming a killed session, a pane can stay stuck at `transcriptStatus: 'loading'` forever; a manual reload unsticks it. Two write paths can each silently drop an in-flight initial-history load's terminal status write:

1. **`loadInitialHistoryForSession`** writes `'loading'` *unconditionally* (`prev[id] ?? emptyRuntime()`) but writes the terminal `'ready'`/`'error'` only inside `if (!current) return prev`. If the runtime entry is dropped or re-keyed (idMap remap) while the load awaits IPC, the terminal write hits a missing key and is thrown away — the surviving runtime stays `'loading'`.
2. **`commitRehydratedState`** rebuilds the runtimes map from a fresh `out = {}` and forces any non-`ready`/`error` status back to `'loading'` for sessions with a `providerSessionId`. If no loader then drives it to `'ready'`, the pane is parked — exactly "stuck until manual reload" (reload re-invokes the loader under a stable id).

## What it adds

- **`transcriptStatusTrace.ts`** (new): `traceTranscriptStatus` appends a `STATE` / `transcript_status` entry (`from -> to @ site`) per transition into the existing per-session `feed-debug.jsonl` — the channel the issue reporter already reads. No parallel log system (consistent with #102's "one debug home"). Two console warns tag the discard and force-to-loading paths with greppable `[transcript-stuck][283]`.
- **`initialHistory.ts`**: trace all four status writes; warn on both `!current` bails *before* they swallow the terminal write.
- **`rehydrate.ts`**: warn when the rebuild drops a still-`loading` old key on re-key, or forces a `providerSessionId` session back to `loading`.

## Safety

Diagnostic only — **no behavior change**. Renderer-only; typechecks clean (`tsconfig.web.json`, 0 errors in touched files). Reproduce once, read the timeline (`feed-debug.jsonl` `transcript_status` series + `[transcript-stuck][283]` console lines), then fix at source and **delete this instrumentation**.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

## ✅ PR #296 — diagnostic instrumentation for #283

**https://github.com/Juliusolsson05/agent-code/pull/296**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Branch** | `fix/283-transcript-status-diagnostics` |
| **Worktree** | `.worktrees/283-transcript-status-diagnostics` (main checkout untouched, still on `main`) |
| **Account** | `Juliusolsson05` ✓ |

| **Typecheck** | renderer (`tsconfig.web.json`): 0 errors in touched files |

### Why instrumentation, not a fix

I followed systematic-debugging's Iron Law and verified the issue's analysis against the live code. Both suspected drop points are real and confirmed:
- `initialHistory.ts` — `'loading'` is written unconditionally but `'ready'`/`'error'` only inside `if (!current) return prev`.
- `rehydrate.ts:374` — `commitRehydratedState` rebuilds from a fresh `out = {}` and forces non-`ready`/`error` back to `'loading'`.

But — exactly as the issue's author found — *which* async interleaving actually fires can't be pinned on paper, and the issue's own _Status_ section prescribes a diagnostic PR as the next step. A blind guess (e.g. patching the `!current` guard) wouldn't cover the id-remap variant. So this PR delivers the timeline; the source fix follows once it reproduces.

### What it captures
- A `transcript_status` series in the per-session `feed-debug.jsonl` (the file the reporter already reads) logging every `from → to @ site` transition — reusing the existing logger, no new debug channel (per #102).
- Greppable `[transcript-stuck][283]` console warns at the two drop points.

**Repro recipe for the next session:** trigger the stuck pane, then read the `transcript_status` entries + `[transcript-stuck][283]` lines — a session showing `→ loading` with no later `initial-history:ready`, or a `discarded 'ready' write` line, names the culprit path. Then fix at source and delete the instrumentation.
